subject: Clarification on derivative rights, transfers, and no-train evidence
messages:
From: Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@healthcore.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: HealthCore Legal <legal@healthcore.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:14:00-05:00
Subject: DPA redlines + no-train/evidence questions

Alex —

Thanks for taking the call yesterday. We reviewed the draft DPA and have a handful of cross-border and derivative-use items we'd like clarified before we move to legal approval. High level: 

- We need an explicit, contract-level no-training commitment for data labeled as "PHI" and certain sensitive categories.
- For any feature that returns or persists prompts/responses, we need clear ownership language and an explicit statement that HealthCore retains IP in customer-submitted prompts and model outputs for its data.
- Evidence: our risk team is asking for a reproducible proof that customer inputs flagged as exempt (no-train) are never used for model improvement — they requested an explanation of the evidence we can expect (audit logs, exportable artifacts, or attestation).
- Subprocessors: we need an updated list and the ability to review subprocessor transfers outside the US/EU.

I've attached our redlines (HealthCore_DPA_redlines_20261112.pdf). Can you confirm which items Redwood can accept as-is, which will need product changes, and what evidence you can provide for the last two bullets?

Appreciate a short mutual action plan (dates) if we can get to agreement.

Regards,
Emma Lopez
Head of Compliance
HealthCore Medical

(attachment: HealthCore_DPA_redlines_20261112.pdf)

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@healthcore.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T12:38:00-05:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines + no-train/evidence questions

Emma —

Thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. Quick answers up front and then a proposed MAP: 

1) No-train commitment: Redwood can provide a contractual no-training commitment for data you designate as "Protected Inputs". That commitment covers both our hosted and Dedicated offerings; for Private/on-prem we can offer a similar contractual guarantee plus code-level controls.

2) Ownership: Our standard language states that customers retain ownership of their inputs and outputs. We can add an explicit clause clarifying that HealthCore retains IP rights over prompts and derived outputs generated from your data.

3) Evidence for non-training: We can provide the following evidence options:
   - Subprocessor access logs (exportable CSVs) showing ingestion and access events
   - Token-level processing trace for sample requests (redacted) to show where data flows in the serving stack
   - An attestation signed by our security team describing that no-training router paths are disabled for Protected Inputs

4) Subprocessors & transfers: We will provide our current subprocessor list and a process for prior notification of material transfers. For transfers outside the EU/US we can offer SCCs plus an option to restrict processing regionally under Dedicated or Private deployments.

Proposed MAP:
- 11/13: Redwood to share updated DPA with explicit no-train and ownership wording (attached) + current subprocessor list + SOC 2 link.
- 11/16: HealthCore to review and flag any remaining product-required changes.
- 11/20: Target final DPA signature or set follow-up call if product changes needed.

I've attached our current DPA template with suggested insertions (Redwood_DPA_template_v3.pdf) and a link to our SOC 2 report. If it's helpful, Karthik (cc'd) can outline the technical evidence options in a follow-up note.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

(attachment: Redwood_DPA_template_v3.pdf)
https://redwood-inference.s3.amazonaws.com/soc2_report_q3_2026.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@healthcore.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T10:07:00-05:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines + no-train/evidence questions

Emma —

Following Alex's summary, a few technical clarifications on the evidence and implementation paths so your risk team can pick the right option: 

- Architecture & enforcement: We support a policy tag on inbound requests ("ProtectedInputs=true"). When set, requests follow a hardened runtime path that disables model-updates, data persistence to training stores, and excludes the KV cache from long-term telemetry aggregation.

- Evidence artifacts we can provide (pick one or more):
  * Exportable access log (CSV) for the account showing ingestion timestamps, worker instance IDs, and subprocessor endpoint IDs for a 90-day window.
  * Sample processing trace: for 5 representative requests, we can provide a redacted token trace showing routing, decision points (cached response vs fresh inference), and confirmation of no-training flags.
  * Signed attestation: short-form statement from our security org describing the runtime guarantees and the exact controls applied.

- KMS & key segregation: If HealthCore wants an additional control, Dedicated deployments support customer-managed keys (CMK) for encrypting any persisted artifacts. For Private/on-prem, keys never leave the customer environment.

- Subprocessor review: We'll send our current list and offer a 30-day review window for any proposed new subprocessor that will process Protected Inputs. If a proposed subprocessor is unacceptable, we can discuss migration to Dedicated or Private modes to avoid that subprocessor.

If helpful I can prepare a short appendix that maps each requested evidence item to the log fields we will provide (format + retention). Happy to jump on a 30-min technical call with your risk team.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Applied ML & Inference Safety
karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com

Alex / Karthik —

This is exactly the level of detail our team needed. A couple quick confirmations before we proceed to redline acceptance: 

1) Attestation scope: please confirm attestation includes a high-level description of the runtime path and that Protected Inputs are excluded from any model improvement pipelines.
2) Evidence export: we'll take the exportable access log + 5 redacted traces. Please confirm format (CSV + JSON) and retention (90 days).
3) Subprocessor process: 30-day review window is acceptable. For transfers outside the EU/US we will expect SCCs; in material cases we will ask for Dedicated deployment as a fallback.

Assuming those confirmations, we will sign the attached DocuSign envelope for the amended DPA and aim for signature by 11/20 per the MAP. I'll loop in procurement for the Docusign.

Thanks everyone — pleased we could get to a practical path.

Best,
Emma Lopez
Head of Compliance
HealthCore Medical
